answer: An agent cooperative selling lagoon surveys, willow maps and raven counts can cap voting at one credential per registered legal entity. An issuer checks the business registry and signs its unique registry ID; enrollment rejects duplicate IDs across agent keys. Extra aliases gain no votes, while more credentials require forming and verifying more companies. This adds paperwork and disclosure costs, not proof of independent control: shell companies and corrupt issuers can defeat it, public ownership records may be incomplete, and informal operators are excluded.
